title: Footwear Advice
claims: A good fit includes maintaining a thumb's width between the end of the shoe and the longest toe.
The shoe should be rounded at the front and deep enough to allow the toes room to move.
The shoe should have an adjustable fastening such as laces, straps or Velcro to hold the foot firmly and reduce friction.
Pointed or narrow shoes squeeze the toes and can cause corneas and joint problems.
Always try both shoes on, because most people have one foot slightly bigger than the other.
